title: Office Space Planning for Newcastle Not-for-Profits
excerpt: A practical framework for community organisations assessing office space, lease commitments and stakeholder needs.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Newcastle Office Planning for Not-for-Profits | YOS
metaDescription: A practical office and lease planning guide for not-for-profit organisations in Newcastle and the Hunter.
body:
Not-for-profit organisations often need to balance service delivery, accessibility, funding conditions, workforce needs and long-term commitments. A written property brief helps make those trade-offs visible.

## Start with service delivery

Map who uses the premises, when they attend, privacy needs, accessibility, public transport, parking, storage, security and any specialist rooms or services.

## Confirm approval and funding constraints

Identify board approvals, grant conditions, budget cycles, procurement rules and evidence required for the decision. Build these into the timetable.

## Compare total cost and flexibility

Review occupancy costs, fitout, relocation, reinstatement, review mechanisms, expansion or contraction and exit options. Test scenarios rather than relying on one forecast.

## Coordinate specialist advice

Commercial, legal, financial, planning, accessibility and technical questions require the appropriate qualified advisers. Keep an issues register so nothing is lost between parties.

## Ask about support before assuming it

The scope and fees for any engagement should be confirmed in writing before work begins. Do not rely on an expired promotion or an informal offer.

Your Office Space can discuss the requirement, define an appropriate scope and help coordinate the property process for Newcastle and Hunter organisations.
